subject: How are the starting values calculated in lavaan?

messages.author: ab08386cc5e71286
messages.subject: How are the starting values calculated in lavaan?
parts:
Hello,
I was wondering how the starting values of the likelihood function are calculated in R lavaan for ML Estimation. I have heard that most programs (e.g., LISREL) systematically choose their starting values (instead of randomly). Is this the case for R lavaan as well? If so, how are they calculated? 

Thanks in advance,
Noell

messages.author: db13c3b329e98ebb
messages.subject: Re: How are the starting values calculated in lavaan?
parts:
Dear Noell,

In lavaan 0.6-15, by default, the factor loadings are initialized using FABIN3 (Hägglund, 1982). The residual variances of the observed indicators are set to half of the observed variance, and the latent variances are set to 0.05. Covariances and regression coefficients are initialized to zero. So indeed, no random starting values are employed.

Kind Regards,
Julie

Hägglund, G. , (1982). Factor analysis by instrumental variables methods. Psychometrika, 47, 209–222

messages.author: b8fd92e5e3662745
messages.subject: Re: How are the starting values calculated in lavaan?
parts:
Some other meaningful starting values can come from say instrumental variable estimators (Bollen's long, long thread of contributions; I was fortunate to hop on that train of thought for a couple of those). I initialized my Stata -confa- CFA program (https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1536867X0900900301) with the instrumental variable estimates (with semi-meaningful residual variances like half of the marginal variance), I have seen far more stable convergence than random starting values or zeroes. lavaan is open source... steal my idea and PR it and make yourself famous.
